title: Adaptive-sampling-eval-bridge-for-config-led-model-advances
creator: Ana Rodriguez
description:
Problem: Catalog updates and tenant-level model pins/config changes currently trigger full-fidelity eval runs or ad-hoc smoke checks, leading to high cost and slow feedback. We need a system that runs targeted, budget-aware quality checks when model versions or serving configs change so operators can catch regressions quickly without burning eval budget.

Goal: Implement an 'eval bridge' that listens to model-version and config change events (catalog promotions and tenant pin upgrades), spawns lightweight, adaptive-sampling eval jobs, and surfaces differential quality signals to the Console and rollout controller. The bridge should prioritize tenants with high risk profiles and track signal quality over time to inform rollouts and automated rollback decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge subscribes to catalog and tenant-pin events and enqueues eval jobs within 60s of the event
Adaptive sampler selects representative prompts and traffic slices with a configurable budget cap per change
Differential metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/LLR/custom scoring) and a signal confidence score are emitted to the Console and an alerting webhook
Cost throttling prevents eval spend for a tenant from exceeding configurable monthly budget
Bridge exposes an operator endpoint to re-run targeted evals and to mark a change as safe/unsafe
updates: 2026-03-01: Drafted ticket and scoped MVP with Eng. Focus on catalog promotions + tenant pin upgrades first.
2026-03-04: Design sync with Runtime team — decided to use existing event bus (change-event-v2) and reuse sampling library from evals-service to avoid duplication.

2026-03-06: Prototype run for a catalog promotion (gpt-large-v2 -> gpt-large-v3) showed a 0.6% NLL regression on a 2k-sample but high variance for low-traffic tenants. Added tenant-prioritization weighting to prototype.

2026-03-09: Spike result: adaptive sampler reduced token cost by ~74% vs full run while still surfacing the regression for medium+traffic tenants. Created PR: github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/2483.

2026-03-11: Review notes from Reliability: must include retry/backoff for event delivery and a hard budget fallback (skip eval when budget exhausted). Also require audit log entries for every automatic eval run.

2026-03-12: Design doc updated with operator controls and cost throttle. Blocker opened: need tenant sampling whitelist from Product (PM-61234) to avoid running on sensitive customers without approvals.
notes: Trade-offs: heavy sampling yields better confidence but high cost. We prioritize signal for tenants with higher traffic, SLAs, or preexisting alerts.
Decision: start with read-only analysis (no auto-rollback) for the first release; auto-rollback will be considered in a follow-up after we validate false-positive rates.
Edge cases: quantization config changes may alter tokenization or logits distributions; include a preflight step that verifies model schema compatibility before running evals.
next_steps: Finalize event schema and contract with Runtime (owner: Marcus Lee)
Implement budgeted adaptive sampler in evals-service (owner: ENG-30217)
Add Console panel for per-change eval diffs with signal confidence and links to raw examples (owner: UI team)
Run controlled canary on internal tenants and monitor false positive/negative rates for two weeks
